newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Continental to resume Venezuela flights after 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Continental to resume Venezuela flights after 15 years.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. said Tuesday it will resume direct flights to Venezuela on Oct. 1 after an absence of 15 years.
The initial service will be between Houston and Caracas, it said.

The new route is aimed at capitalising on the important oil and petrochemicals links opening up between the two cities, Ralph Shulz, vice president of sales and marketing for Latin America, told a news conference.
Continental plans to add a New York-Caracas service in 1998, said Andrew Czobor, director of planning and strategy for Latin America.
The Caracas-Houston route is expected to carry an average of 104 passengers per day and turn a profit of about $5.6 million per year, Czobor said.
Caracas will be Continental's 26th destination in Latin America. The company plans to add a New York-Sao Paulo-Rio de Janeiro route July 10, the airline said.
